name: Azithromycin
route_note: Oral tablets or suspension (often 3- or 5-day courses or single dose), IV infusion, and eye drops.
targets: 23S rRNA of the 50S ribosomal subunit (nascent peptide exit tunnel)

discovery.by: Gabrijela Kobrehel, Gorjana Radobolja-Lazarevski and Zrinka Tamburašev, led by Slobodan Đokić (Pliva)
discovery.note: Made by inserting a methylated nitrogen into the erythromycin lactone ring, producing a 15-membered azalide with better acid stability and tissue penetration.

tagline: Long-acting azalide used for respiratory infections, STIs and mass drug administration
summary: Azithromycin is a semi-synthetic azalide discovered at Pliva in Zagreb and licensed to Pfizer as Zithromax. Its long tissue half-life allows short courses, making it one of the world's most widely used antibiotics for respiratory infections, chlamydia, trachoma and enteric infections.
mechanism: Azithromycin binds the 23S rRNA in the peptide exit tunnel of the 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibits translation; it is mainly bacteriostatic, but bactericidal against some organisms at high concentrations.

The ring nitrogen improves activity against Haemophilus influenzae and some Gram-negative enteric pathogens. Azithromycin accumulates extensively in tissues and phagocytes, which carry it to sites of infection. It also has immunomodulatory effects exploited in cystic fibrosis and bronchiectasis.
uses: Community-acquired pneumonia and atypical pathogens (Mycoplasma, Chlamydophila, Legionella)
Acute exacerbations of COPD and sinusitis
Chlamydia trachomatis and trachoma (mass drug administration)
Traveller's diarrhoea, Campylobacter and Shigella infections, typhoid
Mycobacterium avium complex prophylaxis and treatment
Long-term prophylaxis in cystic fibrosis and bronchiectasis (off-label in some regions)

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Pliva researchers synthesise azithromycin; a patent is filed in 1981.

history.title: Pfizer licence
history.detail: Pliva licenses the compound to Pfizer for Western markets.

history.title: First launch
history.detail: Pliva launches Sumamed in Central and Eastern Europe.

history.title: Trachoma donation
history.detail: Pfizer and the Edna McConnell Clark Foundation found the International Trachoma Initiative to donate azithromycin for trachoma elimination.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: US patent expiry leads to generic azithromycin.

history.title: Cardiac warning
history.detail: The FDA warns that azithromycin can cause fatal heart rhythms, following a 2012 NEJM cohort study.

history.title: MORDOR trial
history.detail: Biannual mass azithromycin distribution reduces childhood mortality in Niger, Malawi and Tanzania (NEJM).

pk.metabolism: limited hepatic metabolism; weak CYP3A4 inhibitor

serious: QT prolongation and torsades de pointes
Infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis in neonates

facts: Azithromycin was one of the first major drugs discovered in a socialist-era Eastern European laboratory and licensed to a Western company.
Mass distribution of azithromycin is a cornerstone of WHO's SAFE strategy against trachoma.
